title: Post-Train NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge for On-Device Robot Control | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 Edge, a 4B-parameter world-model-based policy small enough to run fully on Jetson Thor, achieves 22.9% success in closed-loop RoboLab manipulation benchmarks after post-training on the Cosmos3-DROID dataset, running with no data-center GPU in the loop but trading accuracy versus the larger Cosmos 3 Nano (36.8% success) for real-time, on-device autonomy.

themes.theme: On-device robot policy deployment via Cosmos 3 Edge

insights.claim: Cosmos 3 Edge is a 4B-parameter omni-model (with a 2B NVIDIA Nemotron-based reasoner) in the Cosmos 3 family, pretrained on the same physical-world data as Cosmos 3 Nano and Cosmos 3 Super, but small enough to run entirely on NVIDIA Jetson Thor with no data-center GPU required.
insights.speaker: Saeed Babamohamadi
insights.so_what: Signals NVIDIA is productizing a tiered family of world-foundation models sized for different deployment envelopes (data center vs. edge robot), extending its platform strategy from GPUs into embodied-AI software stacks.

insights.claim: The post-trained Cosmos 3 Edge policy, running on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor T5000, generates each 32-action chunk in about 1.53 seconds while a chunk covers roughly 2.13 seconds of robot motion, allowing continuous arm movement with no data-center GPU in the loop because the next chunk is ready before the current one finishes.
insights.speaker: Saeed Babamohamadi
insights.so_what: Demonstrates a working real-time on-device inference budget for robot control, a concrete latency benchmark investors can use to compare against competing edge-AI/robotics compute platforms.
insights.locator: The DROID action policy runs in real time

insights.claim: In closed-loop RoboLab evaluation across 120 language-conditioned manipulation tasks, the post-trained Cosmos 3 Edge policy reaches 22.9% success, versus 36.8% for the larger Cosmos 3 Nano, at a fraction of the inference compute -- an explicit trade-off NVIDIA frames as the intended design for real-time, fully on-robot autonomy.
insights.speaker: Saeed Babamohamadi
insights.so_what: Quantifies the accuracy cost of shrinking a world model for edge deployment; investors evaluating physical-AI/robotics plays should weight success-rate benchmarks against compute/latency claims rather than treating on-device capability as free.
insights.locator: In closed-loop RoboLab evaluation, the post-trained Edge policy reaches 22.9% success

insights.claim: At roughly 9 GB in BF16, Cosmos 3 Edge policy weights fit within Jetson Thor's on-board memory, allowing both the policy server and control client to run on the robot itself with the WebSocket request never leaving the device (host="localhost").
insights.speaker: Saeed Babamohamadi
insights.so_what: Establishes a concrete memory footprint benchmark (9GB BF16) that competing edge inference chips/platforms would need to match to host comparable robot foundation models on-device.
insights.locator: Because the server runs on Thor, host="localhost"

insights.claim: The release policy trains on the nvidia/Cosmos3-DROID dataset, containing 76,000 successful teleoperated trajectories (~350 hours across 86 tasks and 564 scenes) collected with a Franka Panda arm and Robotiq gripper, packaged in LeRobotDataset v3.0 format.
insights.speaker: Saeed Babamohamadi
insights.so_what: Defines the scale of proprietary teleoperated demonstration data NVIDIA is releasing/using to bootstrap robot foundation models, a moat component alongside compute for physical-AI competitors to match.
insights.locator: What data does the policy train on?

insights.claim: Post-training Cosmos 3 Edge is foundation-model-scale, not a single-GPU fine-tune: the validated run uses 64 nodes of 4x NVIDIA GB200 Grace Blackwell Superchips for 60K iterations, roughly 68 hours (~17.4K GB200-hours).
insights.speaker: Saeed Babamohamadi
insights.so_what: Quantifies real compute demand (~17.4K GB200-hours) for post-training a robot foundation model, a data point for estimating NVIDIA's data-center GPU revenue exposure tied to physical-AI/robotics workloads even when the final deployment target is an edge chip.
insights.locator: This is foundation model post-training, not a single-GPU fine-tune

themes.theme: Beyond robot control: synthetic data generation

insights.claim: Post-training techniques for robot control extend to synthetic data generation: Aigen post-trained Cosmos to generate diverse synthetic crop and weed variations, enabling an autonomous weeding system to achieve strong performance using just 1% real-world training data.
insights.speaker: Saeed Babamohamadi
insights.so_what: A concrete customer proof point showing Cosmos-based synthetic data can drastically cut real-world data collection needs (100x less), relevant for agtech/robotics companies evaluating NVIDIA's world-model tooling to reduce data-acquisition costs.

insights.claim: Cosmos is released with open weights and framework under the OpenMDW1.1 license, which the author frames as making post-training an accessible route to building specialized physical-AI models.
insights.speaker: Saeed Babamohamadi
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's open-licensing strategy for Cosmos lowers adoption friction versus closed competing world-model platforms, potentially accelerating ecosystem lock-in to NVIDIA hardware/tooling even as the model itself is open.
insights.locator: Cosmos's open weights and framework, with the OpenMDW1.1 license
